title: kate-core: append to, read, and clear a journal file
summary: start_journal writes the header line to a new journal file. append_journal adds one line and flushes it. read_journal returns the header and every well-formed line and stops at a damaged tail. clear_journal removes the file and treats a missing file as done.

lane.reason: Either lane may code this packet. It is one file, one behavior, and one test, and the rule text in this packet is the oracle. The first idle lane takes it.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: Use OpenOptions append for append_journal. The four functions are pub in recovery.rs and carry #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))] until the stash packet exports them from lib.rs. The test a_journal_file_appends_and_reads uses tempfile::tempdir, starts a journal with header_line, appends two journal lines and one damaged line x, asserts read_journal gives the header path and two lines, and that clear_journal twice is Ok and the file is gone. Do not nest an if inside an if. When two arms return the same value, write one condition with ||. Add each new test at the end of the one test module of the file, before its closing brace; create that module when the file is new. Do not write a second mod tests. An item with no caller outside tests gets #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]; the packet that adds the caller removes it. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: recovery::tests::a_journal_file_appends_and_reads
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because the functions do not exist. After the change two lines read back, a damaged tail is dropped, and a second clear is Ok.
